description: Tests the CHOREOGRAPHY of the real `/run-pipeline` command, not agent quality. A real session runs `/run-pipeline withdraw-money` over a pre-seeded approved spec; the workers (architect/developer/reviewers) are FAKE agent definitions (project-local .claude/agents overrides) that record their own invocation to pipeline-calls.log and return canned artifacts. The fake test-reviewer FORCES a FAIL on the first review (then PASS) so the fix pass is exercised on demand — something real agents won't do reliably. We assert the dance from the call log: plan before implement, implement before review, FAIL triggers a developer fix pass, re-review after the fix, and it stops after a passing review (no further fix). Invoking the real command (not prose) means this tests the production artifact. Paid + pass@k (the session is a real model); faking the workers makes it cheap and the FAIL path forceable. The full CLAUDE.md chain (/intent-and-goal → /run-pipeline) with REAL workers is the separate, opt-in Phase 1d e2e.

when.command:
/run-pipeline withdraw-money

Use the project's architect, developer, and reviewer sub-agents — do not do their work yourself. Work directly in this directory; skip any worktree step. Run non-interactively: do not ask questions and auto-continue.
